minutes.headline: Select Board leans toward letting town meeting voters decide on continued mosquito-control funding.
minutes.summary: The select board approved a one-day liquor license, then held a joint meeting with the board of health for an extensive educational presentation by Central Mass Mosquito Control Project on its surveillance, ditch-maintenance, larval and adult mosquito control work, amid a town budget shortfall that has put the district's assessment on the table. No vote was taken on the mosquito control funding; the chair said it should go to town meeting voters. The board also acknowledged a Conservation Commission resignation, heard a brief town manager report on a building leak, and reviewed (without voting on) draft warrant articles for the 2026 annual town meeting before recessing into a tri-board meeting.

watch_next: Whether mosquito-control funding appears as a warrant article for a town meeting vote
Final warrant articles for the 2026 annual town meeting, including the draft revolving-fund and capital-cleanup items reviewed this meeting

what_happened.line: The select board chair said continued funding for mosquito control should be decided by town meeting voters, not the board, amid a town budget shortfall.
No vote was taken on the mosquito control assessment; the board instead held a joint educational session with the board of health on the program.
The board approved a one-day liquor license for the Lunenburg Diner for a March 19 event.

The board reviewed, but did not vote on, draft 2026 town meeting warrant articles covering a new Economic Development revolving fund, a technology revolving fund renaming, an FY26 capital cleanup item, and vacation buyout transition language.
The board acknowledged a resignation from the Conservation Commission.

why_it_matters: If mosquito control funding goes to town meeting, residents will be asked to vote directly on whether to keep paying into that regional assessment, which a board member said the state sets using a land-mass and valuation formula rather than local choice.

The draft warrant articles reviewed -- a new revolving fund, a capital reallocation, and a policy change to vacation buyouts -- are early-stage and not yet committed to the warrant, but they preview what voters may see at the 2026 annual town meeting.
A public commenter raised a concern about pesticide safety to bees, which residents may want addressed before any funding vote.
